transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-12 11:00 PT
- Duration: ~32 minutes
- Attendees: Liam (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcos (CSM); Ellen, Samir, Dana, Tom (Blue Mesa)

Auto Summary (auto-gen may be partial):
Runbook and security handshake; discuss staging VPC, SOC2 docs, KMS integration, and benchmark plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam Carter: hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick roll call — we got Ellen, Samir, Dana, Tom from Blue Mesa?
[00:12] Ellen Park: yes that's us. thanks Liam.
[00:15] Priya Nair: awesome, i'll be the SE on this one — i'll lead the runbook walkthrough and the benchmark plans.
[00:22] Samir Khan: great. our main ask today is to make sure we can validate latency SLOs in our staging VPC and confirm security posture before prod.
[00:28] Priya Nair: totally, we'll cover access, peering, and the short smoke bench. quick note — we will be provisioning a Redwood staging tenant on dedicated infra for the pilot, unless you prefer hosted. any preference?
[00:40] Tom Reed: leaning dedicated for predictability, but we need private peering. we can't route through public endpoints for the PII flows.
[00:46] Dana Lewis: and we need to see audit logs for every request, plus KMS integration so keys never leave our control. SOC2 is table stakes.
[00:54] Marcos Gutierrez: understood. we can do private VPC peering or VPC endpoints depending on your cloud. we also have an on-prem package if needed but looks like peering is fine for now.
[01:05] Ellen Park: timeline wise, we want a canary in prod in ~6 weeks. success metric is p95 latency under 250ms for our chat flows at 50 rps and cost per 1k tokens within the target.
[01:18] Priya Nair: that's clear. for the benchmark we'll need your sample payloads and the expected QPS. Tom, can you share the sample traces?
[01:25] Tom Reed: yes, i'll drop a small set in the shared drive. also note some of our requests hit long context windows — up to 4k tokens.
[01:33] Priya Nair: good to know. that affects kernel selection and KV cache behavior; we'll note warm-up profiles.
[01:40] Samir Khan: question on encryption — will Redwood call out to our KMS for every token, or is there session-level wrapping?
[01:47] Marcos Gutierrez: we do envelope encryption; the runtime uses customer-managed keys for at-rest model artifacts and request logs can be wrapped by your KMS. per-request decrypt is avoided; we maintain session keys.
[01:58] Dana Lewis: can you send a diagram? that's important for our auditors — specifically how keys are rotated and where logs land.
[02:04] Liam Carter: yes, i'll include the key rotation diagram in the security bundle.
[02:09] Ellen Park: another concern is fallback behavior — if dedicated nodes saturate, will requests fall back to a hosted variant? we need explicit data flow and data residency guarantees.
[02:19] Priya Nair: we can configure a no-fallback policy for your tenant to prevent any cross-tenant routing. alternatively, you can allow region-only fallback inside your VPC. we'll add the routing policy options to the runbook.
[02:30] Tom Reed: good. also, can we pre-warm model caches for expected peak hours? we have daily peaks.
[02:36] Priya Nair: yes, we support scheduled pre-warm jobs and prefix caching. for long contexts caching behavior needs a bit of tuning. we'll include tuning knobs and default values.
[02:46] Samir Khan: what's the expected lead time to provision staging dedicated capacity?
[02:50] Marcos Gutierrez: roughly 48 hours after we get the onboarding info and VPC details; if you want faster we can do a temporary hosted sandbox for bench runs.
[02:58] Dana Lewis: sending VPC ranges and firewall policy by Tuesday. also, Dana: we require SAML SSO integration and RBAC matrix before production.
[03:06] Liam Carter: noted — we have a standard SAML SSO doc and RBAC template. i'll share those and the SOC2 self-attestation docs.
[03:14] Ellen Park: about cost controls — can Redwood limit tokens or throttle to avoid surprises in early runs?
[03:20] Priya Nair: yes, quota policies per token and per-route plus burst limits. we'll propose a conservative policy for the first canary.
[03:27] Tom Reed: competitor check — we've looked at Anthropic host offerings and our internal infra. can Redwood show cost vs latency curves for our expected profile?
[03:36] Priya Nair: we can run the same payloads through a short benchmark and produce a token-level cost & latency breakdown; we'll include quantized model variants if applicable.
[03:46] Samir Khan: perfect. on compliance, vendor attestation — do you have a SOC2 cert we can share?
[03:52] Marcos Gutierrez: yes, SOC2 Type II certificate and penetration test report — i'll put both in the bundle.
[03:57] Dana Lewis: also need an inventory of third-party subprocessors.
[04:01] Liam Carter: included.
[04:03] Priya Nair: demo note — during the benchmark window we'll run 3 passes: cold start, warmed cache, and peak bursts. estimate each pass 10-12 minutes.
[04:12] Ellen Park: ok that'll fit in the 1-hr slot.
[04:15] Tom Reed: tiny nit — when you say "dedicated" what GPU family are we talking about? we saw notes about A100 vs H100 in the model catalog.
[04:23] Priya Nair: default is A100 Perf profile; for LLAMA-like models H100 is an option and we can recommend quantization profiles. we'll call out model/hardware mapping in the runbook.
[04:33] Samir Khan: any required agents or proxies to install in our VPC?
[04:37] Marcos Gutierrez: no agents — we use VPC peering and a small NAT/endpoint for control plane. no inbound opens.
[04:45] Dana Lewis: good. final thing — audit log retention: can we set 7 years? that's our default retention for some logs.
[04:52] Liam Carter: we have configurable retention; 7 years is possible via long-term archive to your chosen bucket with customer-managed lifecycle rules. we'll assemble details.
[05:02] Ellen Park: great, sounds like we're aligned. to recap next steps?
[05:06] Marcos Gutierrez: i'll send the security bundle (SOC2, pen test, subprocessors) by Monday the 14th.
[05:11] Priya Nair: i'll send a staging runbook draft and bench plan by Wednesday the 16th.
[05:16] Tom Reed: i'll share payloads and peering ranges by Tuesday the 15th.
[05:20] Dana Lewis: i'll review the RBAC and SAML checklist once you send it.
[05:24] Liam Carter: ok meet again after the bench run — we'll schedule the 1-hr benchmark slot next week. thanks everyone.
[05:31] Ellen Park: thanks all. bye.

End of transcript.
